description: Discovery vectors: the PresenceRecord key=value encoding shared by mDNS TXT and the UDP beacon, and the UDP beacon frame header. See ProjectInfo/04-PROTOCOL.md section 3.
derivation: Assembled from section 3.1/3.2 by an independent PowerShell script linking against neither implementation. pk8 was computed with .NET SHA-256 over the documented domain-separated input. The public key used is the all-zero key from identity/device-id.json, so this file and that one describe the same hypothetical device.

encoding.pairs: key=value lines joined with \n, UTF-8, at most 400 bytes
encoding.order: v, id, pf, cap, pk8, tok, p, then n if present, then pk if present
encoding.cap: capability bits in lower-case hexadecimal, no 0x prefix
encoding.pk: base64url of the 32-byte X25519 static public key, unpadded

expected.payloadText:
v=1
id=6JE8415YZQQYQMBD34569HVYX4
pf=windows
cap=1f
pk8=0efbac270507d720
tok=0102030405060708
p=47650
n=Test PC
pk=AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA

presenceVectors.name: Private mode omits name and public key entirely
presenceVectors.note: Omitted, never sent empty. An empty value still tells an observer that a name exists and is being withheld (REQ-D06).

expected.payloadText:
v=1
id=6JE8415YZQQYQMBD34569HVYX4
pf=windows
cap=1f
pk8=0efbac270507d720
tok=0102030405060708
p=47650

beaconVectors.name: Bare QUERY, the smallest legal frame
beaconVectors.note: A query with no payload is legal: it means 'announce yourselves' and nothing more.

beaconVectors.name: ANNOUNCE carrying the full public-mode record

rejectionVectors.name: declared length longer than the datagram is rejected
rejectionVectors.note: This is the classic parser bug, and in a network-facing decoder it is a read past the end of received data.

input.mutate: set payloadLength to 0xFFFF, leave the frame unchanged

rejectionVectors.name: the received length is authoritative, not the buffer size
rejectionVectors.note: A UDP receive hands back a fixed-size buffer plus a separate length. Using the buffer size reads uninitialised tail as payload.

input.setup: copy a valid 166-byte frame into a 2048-byte buffer

rejectionVectors.name: foreign traffic is rejected on the magic
a version other than 1 is refused, not guessed
ANNOUNCE with an empty payload is invalid
a duplicate key is rejected
rejectionVectors.note: Two conflicting claims. Picking either silently would let an attacker get a different reading on the two platforms.

rejectionVectors.name: a name containing a bidi override is rejected
rejectionVectors.note: Bidi overrides reorder rendered text, so a hostile device could advertise a name that displays as a trusted one (REQ-U04).

rejectionVectors.name: a name longer than 32 UTF-8 bytes is rejected

notes: Presence carries no authority. It answers only 'which IP:port might be a Veyro peer?'. An attacker can broadcast a record claiming any deviceId; the connection then fails because they do not hold the private key (REQ-D07).
Unknown keys must be ignored rather than rejected, so a newer peer adding a field does not break an older one.
The payload is capped at 400 bytes, which mirrors mDNS TXT record size reality and bounds the UDP beacon.
pk8 exists so a browser can pre-filter cheaply without parsing the whole record.
